headline: Scale is relative—what seems large from one perspective is tiny from another, and behavior changes at different scales
universal_truth: Context determines significance; size only matters in comparison
fun_facts: A bacterium is to you as you are to a planet—the scale difference is similar
Ants can carry 50 times their body weight, but if they were human-sized, they'd collapse under their own weight
Water behaves differently at small scales—insects can walk on it because surface tension dominates
discussion_questions: What seems big in your life that would seem small from a different perspective?
How does zoom level change what you notice?
At what scale do your problems matter most?

hook.script: You're huge compared to ants, tiny compared to mountains, microscopic compared to planets. There is no absolute big or small—only comparison. And at different scales, the rules change. What works small often fails large, and vice versa.

cliff.script: We assume a larger version of something behaves the same as a smaller version. But physics changes at different scales. Why doesn't everything scale linearly?
cliff.prompt: Why do things behave differently at different scales?

options.text: Volume grows faster than surface area—doubling size increases weight 8x but surface only 4x, changing which forces dominate
options.response: Yes. This is the square-cube law. It's why ants can't be elephant-sized—their legs would snap. And why elephants can't jump—they can't generate enough force relative to their weight.

options.text: Different materials have different scaling properties
options.response: Materials matter, but the geometry of scaling affects everything...

fact1.title: Square-Cube Law
fact1.script: Double the size of something and surface area quadruples (2²) but volume goes up eight times (2³). This means larger creatures have proportionally less surface area. They can't cool as easily, can't support their weight as easily. Size brings constraints.

fact2.title: Dominant Forces
fact2.script: Different forces dominate at different scales. At tiny scales, surface tension rules—insects walk on water. At large scales, gravity dominates—whales beach helplessly. The physics you experience depends on your size.

fact3.title: Zoom and Focus
fact3.script: What you notice depends on your zoom level. Zoom in on skin and you see cells. Zoom out from Earth and countries vanish. Scale determines what's visible and what's important. The 'right' perspective depends on what you're trying to understand.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Context determines significance. Scale teaches that size only matters in comparison. Your problems are small cosmically but large personally—both are true. Choose the scale that helps.

outro.script: That's Day 179. Tomorrow, we'll explore why difference catches your eye—contrast. Until then, play with scale: zoom in and out mentally on something familiar and notice what appears and disappears.

growTrack.title: Scale Shifting - Zoom In and Out
growTrack.learning_objective: Practice viewing issues at different scales
growTrack.activity: Take something that concerns you and view it at different scales: zoom in (what are the immediate details?) and zoom out (how does this look in 10 years? From someone else's life? Cosmically?). Different scales reveal different truths.
